chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya told me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, who said: Abu Sa'id al-Mada'ini told me, attributing it to the Prophet (or Imam) regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "Then Adam received from his Lord, Words" He said: I asked him by the right of Muhammad, Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn, peace be upon them.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (referring to Muhammad, Ali, Fatima, Hasan, and Husayn)
key_terms.بِحَقِّ: By the right of (invoking the authority or merit of the Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.كَلِمَاتٍ: Words (plural of kalimah, referring to the specific supplication or phrases)
key_terms.يَرْفَعُهُ: He attributes it (to the Prophet or an Imam, indicating a hadith qudsi or marfu' status)

ai.seo_question: What were the words Adam received from his Lord for repentance?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to elucidate the specific 'words' (kalimat) Adam recited for his repentance in Surah Al-Baqarah, identifying them as an invocation of the right (haqq) of the Ahl al-Bayt. This highlights the Shia theological view that the intercession and spiritual authority of the Prophet and his progeny were instrumental in the acceptance of Adam’s repentance, linking cosmic history directly to the Ahl al-Bayt.
